service_in_active_registration.checkpoint: before registration of victim address as instance

operator_permanently_blocked_from_regist.meaning: the other operator is permanently blocked from registering any agent instance for any service in the future (DoS)
operator_permanently_blocked_from_regist.checkpoint: after attacker registration of victim address as instance

claims.scope: This will permanently block the other operator from registering any agent instance for any service in the future, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) attack.

preconditions.text: An attacker can create a service with many slots for the purpose of the attack.; The service can be created without the intention to push it to deploy, kept at ActiveRegistration state to register instances.; The victim's address is an operator address used to register agent instances.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.

safety.text: An operator address must not be usable as an agent instance address while it is in use as an operator address; it may only be used as an instance address after its registered instance count reaches zero.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.

effects.text: This will permanently block the other operator from registering any agent instance for any service in the future, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) attack.
effects.derivation: Program-generated direct negation witness for the selected safety pattern.

effect_coverage.reason: Program-generated exact coverage for selected direct impact.

assumptions: The operator address is in use as an operator address (registered instance count tracked in ServiceManager).

limitations: The permanent-block impact is encoded as a grounded Boolean because the report provides no more specific observable for the DoS outcome.
The operator registered instance count is bound to a cross-contract ServiceManager mapping that does not yet exist in the vulnerable code; binding risk is high.
